author: Latham, 1790
habitat: 산간 계곡, 호숫가, 혼효림, 활엽수림 등 우거진 숲

months.note: 여름깃과 겨울깃이 같으나 7월쯤에는 색이 엷어지고 등 광택도 줄어든다.

summary: 드물지 않게 찾아오는 여름철새로, 산골짜기와 호숫가, 혼효림, 활엽수림처럼 우거진 숲에서 번식한다. 숲 속 나무 구멍이나 벼랑의 굴을 쓰거나 흙벽, 썩은 나무 기둥에 스스로 구멍을 파고 알을 낳으며, 암수가 번갈아 품는다. 양서류와 갑각류를 즐겨 먹는다. 전국에 살며 국외에서는 일본, 중국, 필리핀에 분포한다.

points.ko: 꼬리에서 가장 강한 붉은 자색 광택
points.en: violet-red gloss, strongest on the tail

art.subject: Ruddy Kingfisher (Halcyon coromanda), adult (sexes very similar), as seen in shady Korean mountain forest by streams from May to September: head, back, wings and tail rich rufous-orange to cinnamon, with a violet-lilac gloss over the back, wings and especially the tail, the forehead and sides of the head less glossy; a narrow pale silvery-turquoise stripe on the lower back and rump, mostly hidden at rest; chin and upper throat buffy-white; rest of the underparts paler orange-rufous; huge bright coral-red bill; dark eye; red legs and feet.
art.pose: perched on a shaded branch in dense forest by a stream
art.scene: Korean mountain valley in summer with dense broadleaf forest and a stream; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a shaded branch: uniform rufous-orange upperparts with violet gloss strongest on the slightly rounded tail, buffy-white chin and upper throat, huge coral-red bill, red legs
adult in flight, seen from above, head, body and tail in line: rufous wings and back with a narrow pale turquoise stripe down the lower back and rump, violet-glossed tail
adult, head detail in side view: massive red bill, dark eye, buffy-white chin and upper throat, rufous head with little gloss on the forehead and face
art.build: Stocky, large-headed kingfisher, about 27.5cm, much bigger than Common Kingfisher and about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul but far bulkier. Bill enormous, about as long as the head or a little longer, very deep at the base and dagger-shaped. Legs very short, red, with small feet. Short neck; perches upright. Wings short and rounded; the short, slightly rounded tail extends beyond the wingtips. In flight the pale turquoise rump stripe flashes against the rufous back.
avoid: Do not paint a blue back and wings or a white breast - that is Black-capped Kingfisher (Halcyon pileata).
Do not paint a black, small or thin bill; it is huge and red.
Do not paint a long tail or long legs.
Do not paint blue patches on the wings; the blue is only a narrow stripe on the lower back and rump.
